Chapter 10: God’s Immutability—The Anchor in a Changing World.
You know, change is just part of life. People move away, seasons come and go, relationships shift, and even the things we thought were rock-solid can suddenly feel uncertain.
In the middle of all this, the idea that God never changes—it’s kind of amazing, isn’t it? And honestly, there’s something really comforting about that.
Imagine sorting through a box of old photos, seeing how much has changed over the years—familiar faces, favorite places, dreams you once held. There’s this bittersweet feeling, maybe even a longing for something that actually lasts.
That’s where God’s immutability comes in. It’s the promise that, no matter what else shifts around us, He stays the same.
Most of us don’t even realize how much we crave that kind of anchor. When everything else feels up in the air, God’s unchanging nature can be a real source of hope and stability. His character, His promises, His love—they don’t get swept away by the winds of time.
Let me share a story. Picture a family facing a big upheaval—they’re moving to a brand new city, leaving behind everything familiar. Routines are upended, and there’s that nagging anxiety about starting over. But in the middle of all that chaos, they held tight to one belief: God was right there with them, steady and unchanging.
Now, this didn’t magically make everything easy, but it did give them a sense of peace they could lean on.
What really comes through is that God’s immutability isn’t about being distant or untouched by what goes on in our lives. It’s about being faithful, reliable, and trustworthy. Knowing He doesn’t change gives us the courage to face whatever comes next.
Of course, some folks struggle with the idea of an unchanging God in a world that’s always in flux. Maybe they wonder if He’s out of touch, or if He really sees the details of their lives. But the story of faith is all about a God who stays constant and present—someone who steps into our changing world, but isn’t changed by it.
